---
title: "The matrix of pairwise posterior probabilities"
subtitle: "1.13 · after Kline, Rose and Walters (2024), Figure 2A and slides 38 and 54"
description: "Pairwise probabilities under alternative orderings of the same units."
---

Each cell gives $\pi_{ij} = \Pr(\theta_i > \theta_j \mid Y)$, the posterior probability that row $i$ exceeds column $j$ ($1 - \pi_{ij}$ across the diagonal), across alternative unit orderings.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Six sites, by posterior mean.** C above D (.638) sits next to the diagonal (mirror .362); in **Data**, A above B (.812) and E above F (.856) follow.
- **Six sites, by label.** Same order: C above D stays .638.
- **League, by label.** Across 435 pairs, U19 above U25 (.502) is 6 cells from the diagonal (in **Data**: None of these 10 adjacent; farthest 26 cells away).
- **League, by posterior mean.** U19 above U25 moves next to the diagonal, with 8 of these 10 adjacent (farthest 2 cells away in **Data**).
- **Two imprecise units.** At prior SD .10, row U22, column U25 is 5 cells from the diagonal at .528 (both posterior SD .089).

```{=html}
<details>
<summary>Model assumptions and source notes</summary>
<p>The six fictional after-school sites (A to F, from postrank's tutorial data) have normal reading-score posteriors taken as given. The simulated league follows <a href="noisy-league.qmd">Ranking noisy estimates</a> under <a href="shrinkage.qmd">normal&ndash;normal posterior shrinkage</a>; two imprecise units can remain near one half even far from the diagonal. Kline, Rose and Walters (2024) plot these heat maps for first names (Figure 2A; slide 38) and firms (slide 54), putting .5 on the diagonal where postrank leaves it empty.</p>
</details>
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="In postrank"}
```r
library(postrank)
round(1 - pr_tutorial$one$e[, , "score_A"], 3)   # the six sites' matrix (C, D: 0.638)
1 - pr_tutorial$one$e["C", "D", "score_A"]       # 0.6381632
```
:::
